channel.title: Mapping Forward
channel.description: Daily synthesis of articles on cartography, mapping, geospatial data, and geographic intelligence

item.title: BMW Maps Gets 3D Navigation and Driver Assistance Integration via Mapbox
item.description: BMW announced a major BMW Maps update arriving October 2026 with OS X, combining 3D navigation with driver assistance systems in a single screen view — developed with Mapbox to show real-time lane position, road level, and surrounding environment. — Key takeaways: BMW Maps update arriving October 2026 for vehicles equipped with BMW Operating System X ; The update combines 3D navigation with driver assistance systems, showing route, environment, and exact vehicle position in a single view ; Developed in collaboration with Mapbox for more precise environmental representation ; Real-time display includes current lane, road level, and nearby environment through 3D graphics ; Highway Assistant system can assist driving on compatible highways at up to 130 km/h with automatic lane changes ; Semi-automated urban driving assistance planned for 2027 in select markets where regulation permits ; Availability depends on vehicle equipment and local regulations; no timeline for Latin American markets yet

item.title: Maps Are a Starting Point for Responsible Clean Energy Development
item.description: The Nature Conservancy argues that spatial data mapping tools like its Clean Energy Compass are valuable for early-stage renewable energy siting, but relationship-driven community engagement — not data-driven siting — remains the strongest predictor of project success. — Key takeaways: The Nature Conservancy's Clean Energy Compass is an interactive mapping tool for early clean energy planning that incorporates conservation and community considerations ; Mapping tools now include socioeconomic and environmental vulnerability indicators (income, pollution exposure, health burdens, energy affordability) to identify community-level impacts ; Maps can highlight opportunities like brownfields and landfills for renewable energy redevelopment, aligning clean energy goals with land restoration ; Despite their value, maps have limitations: spatial datasets lack local detail, cannot capture community experiences, and may reinforce inequities if used without care ; Early, meaningful community engagement is the strongest predictor of renewable energy project success and long-term acceptance ; Relationship-driven planning, not data-driven siting, is the key to accelerating the clean energy transition

item.title: Google Maps' Misleading Nine-Hour Detour Spells Plummeting Bookings for West Coast Businesses
item.description: Tourism operators on New Zealand's West Coast report cancellations and plummeting bookings because Google Maps is routing drivers on a misleading nine-hour detour, treating a restricted section of State Highway 6 as fully closed when it remains passable. — Key takeaways: Google Maps is treating a restricted section of New Zealand's State Highway 6 as completely closed, routing drivers on a nine-hour detour ; Tourism operators report visitors cancelling bookings due to the misleading routing information ; The restricted SH6 section remains passable, but Google Maps does not reflect this nuance ; The issue highlights the real-world economic impact of mapping errors on local businesses dependent on accurate navigation data ; This is another example of navigation apps causing problems by not accurately reflecting road conditions

item.title: Android Auto: Better Destination Preview Coming to Google Maps with Photos and AI Summaries
item.description: Android Auto version 17.8 brings a redesigned Google Maps destination preview with photos, Gemini AI-generated summaries, and a reworked interface that moves trip time and distance to a bottom bar. — Key takeaways: Android Auto 17.8 update adds photos and AI-generated summaries to Google Maps destination previews, a feature previously only available on smartphones ; Google redesigned the entire UI: trip time and distance now display in a bottom horizontal bar that can be expanded for alternate routes and stops ; Destination photos can be viewed in a dedicated gallery, eliminating the need to check the phone ; A Gemini-generated summary helps drivers confirm the correct destination and anticipate what to expect before arriving ; Features are ready but not yet officially deployed by Google; changes may occur before general availability

item.title: Cameroon Wraps Up Population Census After Two Deadline Extensions, Using Satellite Mapping
item.description: Cameroon completed its 4th General Population and Housing Census after two deadline extensions, deploying 33,000 enumerators with GPS-enabled tablets and high-resolution satellite mapping to locate unrecorded rural settlements — preliminary results expected in five months. — Key takeaways: Cameroon's RGPH-4 census ran from April 24 to September 15, 2026, extended twice by the Prime Minister due to operational hurdles ; Over 33,000 enumerators deployed with encrypted, GPS-enabled mobile tablets for real-time data transmission ; High-resolution satellite mapping was incorporated during the first extension to locate unrecorded rural settlements ; The census was conducted jointly with the General Census of Agriculture and Livestock (RGAE) — a first for Cameroon ; The 2026 census replaces over two decades of projections; the last official census (2005) recorded 17,463,836 inhabitants ; Estimated population prior to census: over 28.8 million; preliminary results expected within five months ; The fully digital CAPI model contrasts sharply with the paper-based 2005 census, whose results took over four years to publish

item.title: Drought in Summer 2026 in 12 Maps and Graphs
item.description: NOAA's National Integrated Drought Information System presents 12 maps and graphs showing that the contiguous US experienced its warmest June-August on record in 2026, with drought covering nearly half the country, record-low reservoir levels, and a historically strong El Niño developing. — Key takeaways: The contiguous US experienced its warmest June-August on record in 2026, exceeding previous records from 1936 and 2021 by 0.4°F ; Drought covered nearly half the country, sustained by below-normal precipitation and above-normal temperatures ; Major western reservoirs Lake Mead and Lake Powell hit all-time record lows ; The extreme conditions fueled a destructive wildfire season with unhealthy smoke levels across large parts of the US ; A potentially historically strong El Niño is projected to continue developing through fall and winter ; Flash drought is worsening in the Southern Plains and Lower Mississippi River Basin ; High evaporative demand was observed across almost every CONUS state, especially Colorado

item.title: High-Resolution European Soil Property Maps Based on LUCAS and AlphaEarth Satellite Embeddings
item.description: Researchers produced 10-meter resolution soil property maps for all of Europe (EU-27 + UK) using machine learning trained on LUCAS soil datasets with AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings, covering soil texture, pH, bulk density, and coarse fragments — a significant leap from the previous 30–250m resolution. — Key takeaways: 10 m resolution soil property maps produced for EU-27 + UK, covering clay, silt, sand content, coarse fragments, pH, and bulk density ; Previous European soil maps ranged from 250 m to 30 m resolution depending on the property; this work closes the resolution gap ; Machine learning workflow trained on LUCAS soil datasets using AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings as predictors ; Artificial Neural Networks outperformed Random Forests, with R² values ranging from 0.21 (coarse fragments) to 0.69 (pH) ; Uncertainty estimate maps were produced using Monte Carlo dropout ; Maps support precision agriculture, soil health assessment at field scale, and spatial planning

item.title: Google Maps affiche enfin la vitesse sans itinéraire actif sur l'écran
item.description: Google deploys a server-side update enabling permanent display of speedometer, speed limits, and stop signs on Android Auto — even without an active navigation route — closing a long-standing gap with Apple CarPlay. — Key takeaways: Google Maps now displays real-time speed, speed limits, and stop signs permanently on Android Auto screens without requiring an active route ; The update is rolling out progressively via server-side flags; users need the latest app version but no manual action ; A recent display bug temporarily removed the speedometer for some users after cache clearing; Google confirmed it was isolated and a fix is being distributed ; Apple CarPlay already had this persistent speed display, highlighting a feature gap Google has now closed

item.title: TomTom Clarifies AFM Register Change Relating to Co-Founders' Shareholding
item.description: TomTom confirmed that a change in the Dutch AFM substantial holdings register regarding co-founders Harold Goddijn and Corinne Vigreux is merely an internal restructuring of how their shares are held — their combined 25.6% position remains unchanged. — Key takeaways: TomTom co-founders Harold Goddijn and Corinne Vigreux restructured how their TomTom shares are held, triggering an AFM register update ; Their total combined position remains 31,971,749 shares, representing 25.6% of total shares — no change in actual shareholding ; The restructuring was reported to the Dutch Authority for the Financial Markets (AFM) in accordance with regulations ; Both co-founders reaffirmed their commitment to TomTom's strategy, technology, and people

item.title: Google Maps Tests New Approach to Prevent Everyone Taking the Same Route
item.description: Google Maps is testing a system that deliberately sends some drivers on different routes to optimize overall network traffic flow rather than individual trip time — early trials show a 2% increase in average speed and 1% reduction in fuel consumption by modifying only 2% of trips. — Key takeaways: Google Maps is experimenting with routing that optimizes global traffic flow rather than each driver's individual fastest path ; The system selectively redirects only some drivers to alternate routes, preventing secondary roads from becoming saturated when a main road has an incident ; Trials in major American cities modified only about 2% of trips but achieved ~2% increase in average speed and ~1% reduction in fuel consumption ; Current GPS apps share a weakness: when an accident or congestion blocks a main road, thousands of drivers receive the same detour, simply moving the problem elsewhere ; The approach represents a shift from individual optimization to network-level traffic management

item.title: Aerial Surveys International Awarded GSA Multiple Award Schedule Contract
item.description: Aerial Surveys International has been awarded a GSA Multiple Award Schedule contract, enabling federal, state, local, and tribal agencies to directly procure its GIS and Earth observation services — including aerial imagery, LiDAR, and geospatial analytics — as a prime contractor. — Key takeaways: Aerial Surveys International (ASIntl) awarded GSA Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) contract for GIS and Earth observation services ; Contract covers SIN 541370GIS (GIS services) and SIN 541370GEO (Earth observation solutions) — placing ASIntl among select contractors authorized for both under a single GSA vehicle ; Federal agencies including USGS, USDA, NOAA, USFS, FEMA, DHS, NGA, and FAA can now issue task orders directly without separate competitive procurement ; ASIntl maintains teaming agreements with 27 partner organizations representing nearly 4,000 professionals ; The award strengthens the TrinityGEO geospatial intelligence framework developed with Polygon Solutions and Urban Hawk ; State, local, and tribal governments also gain direct access for disaster preparedness and emergency response GIS purchases

item.title: Google Maps: Speed Limits and Speedometer Now Display Permanently on Android Auto
item.description: After disappearing for a week, Google Maps' speed limits and speedometer are returning to Android Auto with a new always-on mode that displays even without an active navigation route, though bugs persist for some users. — Key takeaways: Speed limits and the speedometer disappeared from Google Maps on Android Auto for many users, prompting fears of a feature removal ; Google confirmed the disappearance was a temporary bug, not a deliberate rollback of the feature launched in summer 2026 ; A new always-on mode is now rolling out, displaying the speedometer, speed limits, stop signs, and traffic lights without requiring a destination to be set ; The always-on display is particularly useful for daily commutes on familiar routes where full navigation is unnecessary ; Deployment is gradual and not yet available to all users, with Google not specifying a timeline

item.title: Not Google Maps, Not Waze: 5 Navigation App Alternatives for Android Auto
item.description: BGR surveys five navigation apps that work with Android Auto as alternatives to the dominant Google Maps and Waze, covering TomTom, Sygic, OsmAnd, Calimoto, and a resurgent MapQuest. — Key takeaways: TomTom offers free turn-by-turn navigation with Android Auto support, offline maps, EV routing, and an ad-free, privacy-respecting interface ; Sygic provides offline navigation, live traffic, and speed camera alerts, but requires a Premium+ subscription ($20/year) for Android Auto support ; OsmAnd excels at off-road and rural navigation with custom map layers and topographic maps, with Android Auto as a paid feature ($15/year Maps+) ; Calimoto is designed for motorcycle riders with scenic routing, offline maps, and curved-road preference, starting at $13/week ; MapQuest relaunched in March 2026, went viral for refusing to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America, and now supports Android Auto in beta

item.title: BMW and Mapbox Team Up for New 3D View That Makes Driving Easier
item.description: BMW and Mapbox have merged navigation and driver-assistance visuals into a single unified 3D cockpit view, eliminating the disjointed experience of darting between the instrument cluster and center screen. — Key takeaways: BMW Maps now consolidates navigation and driver-assistance graphics into one 3D landscape on the central display ; The system projects the vehicle into a depth-mapped virtual reconstruction of the road, showing the car in its lane with real-time traffic ; BMW developed the visualization layer in-house while licensing Mapbox's mapping engine, acknowledging that automakers rarely make world-class software alone ; The unified view allows drivers to confirm at a glance that the car's AI vision matches reality ; Available on BMW vehicles with Operating System X starting October 2026

item.title: Drug Dealers Listed on Google Maps as Ordinary Businesses
item.description: Drug dealers in France are using Google Maps as a virtual storefront, listing dealing spots as ordinary businesses with addresses, ratings, reviews, and even phone numbers — exposing a major content moderation gap on the world's most popular mapping platform. — Key takeaways: Cannabis dealers are creating fake business listings on Google Maps with precise addresses, star ratings, customer reviews, and contact numbers ; These listings appear as ordinary commercial points of interest to unsuspecting users ; The phenomenon raises serious questions about Google's ability to moderate user-generated business content on its mapping platform ; Law enforcement faces new challenges as drug distribution moves onto mainstream digital platforms ; The case highlights how legitimate mapping infrastructure can be repurposed for illicit commerce

item.title: World Maps Might Soon Get an Upgrade: The UN Votes to Endorse Equal Earth Projection
item.description: The UN General Assembly voted 164-1 to endorse equal-area maps like the Equal Earth projection over the 500-year-old Mercator, which drastically distorts Africa's true size — with only the United States voting against. — Key takeaways: The UN General Assembly passed a resolution on September 4 urging institutions to adopt maps that better represent countries' relative sizes, with 164 votes in favor and only the United States against ; The resolution specifically recommends the Equal Earth projection, developed in 2018, as a fairer alternative to the 1569 Mercator projection ; The #CorrectTheMap campaign, spearheaded by Togo and endorsed by the African Union, argues that the Mercator map diminishes Africa's significance ; The resolution does not ban the Mercator map but urges governments, schools, and tech companies to use equal-area maps where relative landmass size matters ; Togo will be the first country to update its geography textbooks, aiming to do so before the end of 2026

item.title: BMW Dates Urban Hands-Free Driving: 2027, Germany First
item.description: BMW will launch its unified 3D navigation and driver-assistance view in October 2026, with the next step being semi-automated urban driving guided by navigation — hands-free city driving arriving in Germany from 2027. — Key takeaways: From October 2026, BMW Maps on Operating System X combines navigation, environmental perception, and driver-assistance status into a single 3D view on the central screen ; The system places the car in its own lane at the correct road level on multi-level interchanges, drawing traffic from sensors rather than the map ; BMW's next milestone is semi-automated city driving guided by navigation, starting in Germany in 2027 ; Mapbox provides the mapping and rendering layer while HERE supplies the certified high-definition map for redundant lane detection ; The visualization was developed in-house by BMW, running on Mapbox data since Operating System 9 in 2023

item.title: Rhodes College Launches New GIS Undergraduate Certificate Program
item.description: Rhodes College has launched a Geographic Information Science undergraduate certificate, claiming to be the only liberal arts college offering an interdisciplinary GIS credential that bridges sciences, humanities, and arts. — Key takeaways: Rhodes College now offers a 12-credit GIS Undergraduate Certificate, the first interdisciplinary GIS certificate at an independent liberal arts college ; The program includes a foundational course plus electives like Critical Cartographies, Remote Sensing, Mapping Population Health, and Mapping Oral Histories ; GIS skills are increasingly valued across fields including environmental science, urban planning, public health, data analytics, and historic preservation ; The certificate bridges technical skill-building with critical thinking and writing, leveraging the liberal arts context ; Alumni already working in GIS roles report that the combination of hard GIS skills and soft skills from liberal arts training is highly valuable in the job market

item.title: Wildfire Map Spotlight: Brac Island Fire, Croatia
item.description: A major wildfire on Croatia's largest Adriatic island, Brac, has burned over 5,600 hectares — nearly 14% of the island's total area — forcing the evacuation of nearly 700 people, with satellite imagery from Copernicus tracking the fire's spread. — Key takeaways: A wildfire broke out on September 10, 2026, near the village of Ložišće on Brac Island, Croatia ; The fire has burned more than 5,600 hectares, affecting nearly 14% of the island's total area ; Nearly 700 people have been evacuated, including 230 by sea near Milna ; 220 firefighters, 69 fire vehicles, and four Canadair water-bombing aircraft have been deployed ; Strong bora winds have driven the fire's rapid spread toward the southern coast ; Satellite imagery from the EU's Copernicus program has been used to monitor the fire's progression ; The fire spread toward the Blaca desert area and the island's southern coast

item.title: Barranquilla: What to Do About Slow and Congested Mobility, According to TomTom Traffic Index
item.description: Barranquilla ranked as one of the world's slowest and most congested cities in the TomTom Traffic Index 2025, with a 10km trip taking over 36 minutes on average and 46 minutes during evening rush hour, prompting experts to propose solutions from better public transit to parking pricing. — Key takeaways: Barranquilla ranked #1 as the slowest city and #19 for congestion globally in the TomTom Traffic Index 2025 ; A 10km trip took 36 minutes 35 seconds on average, rising to 46 minutes 9 seconds during evening rush hour ; Congestion increased 1.7 percentage points from 61.1% to 62.8% in 2025 ; Barranquilla ranked as the 4th most congested city in Colombia, after Bogotá, Medellín, and Cali ; Expert Isidro Ruiz disputes the global ranking, calling congestion "localized" rather than city-wide ; Road works, canalization, and intersection improvements contribute to temporary congestion ; Proposed solutions include strengthening public transit, limiting building heights, and implementing parking fees in tourist areas

item.title: BMW Maps Displays Navigation and Driver Assistance Information in a Single 3D View
item.description: Starting October 2026, BMW Maps will unify route guidance, surrounding perception, and driver assistance information into a single 3D view on the central display, helping drivers understand both navigation and assisted driving functions in complex traffic situations. — Key takeaways: BMW Maps with driver assistance launches in October 2026 for vehicles equipped with BMW Operating System X ; The 3D view combines navigation, vehicle surroundings, and driver assistance information in one display ; The system shows the vehicle precisely within its lane and at the correct road level ; Highway Assistant 2 enables hands-free driving at up to 130 km/h with automated lane changes via glance confirmation ; The technology was developed by BMW Group, combining precise map data, onboard sensors, and AI, with Mapbox mapping technology support ; Starting in 2027, navigation-guided semi-automated driving will roll out in urban areas, initially in Germany ; The feature covers the entire highway network and the city of Paris at launch, with gradual expansion to other cities

item.title: GPS Navigation and Traffic Concentration: When Everyone Follows the Same Route
item.description: A study published in Nature Communications by researchers from CNR-Isti and the University of Pisa shows that when too many drivers follow GPS navigation simultaneously, route diversity drops by up to 14%, concentrating traffic on the same roads and potentially reversing environmental benefits. — Key takeaways: A Nature Communications study by CNR-Isti and University of Pisa researchers simulated traffic in Florence, Milan, and Rome ; The study integrated GPS data, road network characteristics, and routes from Google Maps, TomTom, Bing Maps, and Mapbox ; Route diversity can decrease by up to 14% when all drivers follow navigation systems ; A critical threshold exists between 60-80% of drivers using navigation, beyond which environmental benefits diminish ; In some Rome scenarios, CO2 reduction benefits completely reversed at high navigation adoption rates ; The problem is the gap between individual optimization and collective outcomes ; Researchers call for algorithms that consider overall city-level effects, not just individual route optimization

item.title: DILRMP 3.0 (2026–2031): Bhu-Aadhaar, GIS Land Records, NAKSHA and Key Features
item.description: India's Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme enters its third phase (2026–2031), creating an integrated GIS-enabled land administration system with unique parcel identification numbers, paperless registration, and cadastral mapping. — Key takeaways: DILRMP 3.0 (2026–2031) is the third phase of India's land-records modernisation programme ; The programme creates an integrated, GIS-enabled, and interoperable land administration system ; Bhu-Aadhaar (ULPIN) provides every geo-referenced land parcel with a 14-digit Unique Land Parcel Identification Number ; GIS and cadastral maps are central to the programme's approach ; NAKSHA scheme supports land survey modernisation ; The programme includes paperless registration and integrated revenue courts ; DILRMP 3.0 shifts from digitising records to creating an integrated digital land-governance ecosystem

item.title: Animated Map Shows Spread of Illegal Israeli Settlements Across Palestine
item.description: Al Jazeera has published an animated map visualizing the spread of illegal Israeli settlements and outposts across Palestine, showing 163 settlements housing 744,700 settlers alongside more than 400 unauthorized outposts by 2024. — Key takeaways: Al Jazeera created an animated visual map showing the spread of illegal Israeli settlements and outposts ; By 2024, 163 illegal settlements housed 744,700 Israeli settlers: 511,100 in the West Bank and 233,600 in East Jerusalem ; More than 400 illegal outposts exist that are not officially counted but are often absorbed into recognized settlements ; The animated map tracks the geographic expansion of settlements over time ; The visualization also documents settler violence accompanying the settlement expansion ; The map serves as a visual explainer of the territorial changes on the ground

item.title: Africa: "Correct The Map" Initiative Adopted by the UN
item.description: The UN General Assembly adopted the "Correct The Map" resolution spearheaded by Togo on behalf of the African Group, a diplomatic milestone that seeks to replace Mercator projection world maps with fairer representations of Africa's true size. — Key takeaways: The UN General Assembly adopted the "Correct The Map" resolution on September 4, 2026, in New York ; The initiative was carried by Togo on behalf of the African Group ; The resolution aims to promote more accurate, balanced, and equitable cartographic representations of Africa ; The initiative challenges the Mercator projection, which distorts the true size of African countries ; While non-binding, the resolution could influence international institutions' map choices ; The Togo and the African Union plan to work together on implementation ; The adoption is seen as a diplomatic victory for Togo and the African Group

item.title: Matrix Geo Solutions Wins Three-Year Adani Infra Contract for Precision Drone Surveying and Geospatial Solutions
item.description: Matrix Geo Solutions, an NSE-listed geospatial technology company, has secured a three-year Annual Rate Contract from Adani Infra for precision drone surveying, LiDAR, GIS, and mapping services across pan-India project locations. — Key takeaways: Matrix Geo Solutions won a three-year Annual Rate Contract (ARC) from Adani Infra ; The contract covers geospatial, LiDAR, surveying, mapping, and allied technology-enabled services ; Services include GIS, digital terrain and surface modelling, infrastructure mapping, and asset intelligence ; The engagement spans pan-India project locations ; Matrix Geo Solutions is an NSE-listed geospatial technology and engineering consultancy ; The company previously completed a 314 km geospatial survey across five highway sections for RITES-NHAI ; The contract highlights the growing role of drone-based surveying in Indian infrastructure

item.title: Google Maps Rolling Out Always-On Speed Limits and Speedometer on Android Auto
item.description: Google Maps is rolling out speed limits, a live speedometer, and traffic signals/stop signs on Android Auto that display even when no destination is set, while also investigating a recent bug that caused the speedometer to disappear for some users. — Key takeaways: Google Maps is rolling out always-on speed limits and speedometer on Android Auto, even without a destination set ; The feature includes traffic signals and stop signs display without active navigation ; The rollout is gradual and not yet available to all users ; A recent bug caused the speedometer to vanish for some Android Auto users, which is being investigated ; Speed limits in Google Maps originally launched in 2019, with the speedometer appearing later ; The feature was previously only visible during active navigation ; The update makes Google Maps more useful for shorter or familiar trips where setting a destination isn't necessary

item.title: There Is No Such Thing as a "UN Map With Borders": Guterres
item.description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres clarified that the UN has never published a map with borders, after India raised "anomalies" about a map used during the "Correct the Map" resolution that omitted Indian and Chinese claim lines in Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin. — Key takeaways: UN Secretary-General Guterres stated categorically: "There is no such thing as a 'UN map with borders'" and "it's not for the UN to define" borders ; The controversial map was created by UN Geospatial during the consultation process for the "Correct the Map" resolution, but Guterres called it "not an official UN map" — "the contribution of an NGO" ; The map depicted Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin without the Indian and Chinese "claim lines" that previous UN maps had used ; India had voted in favor of the "Correct the Map" resolution but raised "anomalies" about the map with the UN ; The map showed the Line of Control in Jammu & Kashmir as a dotted line with an explanatory note, but no similar note for omitted claim lines in Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin ; MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal clarified India's vote was in support of "equal area representation" principle ; Guterres emphasized the resolution itself is not a map but a statement that distortions in landmasses "come from power relations of the past"

item.title: Togo's Faure Gnassingbé Celebrates the "Correct the Map" Resolution Amid Domestic Criticism
item.description: Togolese President Faure Gnassingbé has championed the UN's "Correct the Map" resolution as a triumph for Africa, but critics at home dismiss the celebration as a distraction from two decades of domestic infrastructure failure and political stagnation. — Key takeaways: Togo's President Faure Gnassingbé and Foreign Minister Robert Dussey have positioned themselves as champions of the UN "Correct the Map" resolution ; Critics argue the regime is using the cartographic victory to distract from 20 years of domestic stagnation in infrastructure, healthcare, and development ; The article contrasts Togo's lack of modernization with progress in neighboring West African countries like Benin, Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, and Ghana ; Togo's railway network remains the colonial-era infrastructure, and the promised highway was never built ; The piece highlights the irony of celebrating global cartographic correction while the country's own social and physical landscape remains frozen in the 1960s ; The "Correct the Map" movement is framed as a demagogic project by leaders unable to solve concrete citizen problems

item.title: Australia to Look Bigger on New World Map After Historic UN Vote
item.description: Australia will appear roughly 10% larger relative to northern landmasses under the UN-endorsed Equal Earth projection, as geographer Greg Lauer explains how the shift changes visual perception of the continent's size compared to Greenland and Africa. — Key takeaways: The UN General Assembly voted 164-1 (US opposed) to endorse the Equal Earth projection over the Mercator map ; Australia will appear about 10% larger relative to squeezed northern landmasses — not because Australia grows, but because Greenland shrinks ; Geographer Greg Lauer: "The actual size doesn't change, but Greenland is a lot smaller and you can better see how Australia compares to Africa" ; Africa is 14 times the size of Greenland, but the Mercator map makes them look similar ; The Mercator map "was never wrong — it was right for navigation, but wrong for comparison" ; Where the new map is centred matters: Australia/NZ prefer centring over the Pacific; UK-centred maps distort Australia and push NZ to the edge ; Lauer: "Every flat map lies about something. The honest ones tell you what they're lying about" ; The UN resolution is symbolic — no enforcement mechanism to replace classroom maps

item.title: New World Map Makes Africa Look Bigger: What's the Fuss About? Cartographers Explain
item.description: Cartographers Jack Swab and Derek Alderman explain the UN's endorsement of the Equal Earth projection, why the Mercator map distorts Africa's true size, how the new projection works, and why the US was the lone "no" vote against the resolution. — Key takeaways: The UN passed a non-binding resolution endorsing the Equal Earth projection over the Mercator projection, which exaggerates land towards the poles by 2-14x ; The Mercator projection remains useful for navigation (preserving compass bearings), which is why Google Maps and Apple Maps still use it ; The Equal Earth projection minimizes distortions of continental sizes, making it better for educational, public communication, and policy purposes ; Map-making is decentralized — no single authority regulates which projection is used; the UN endorsement is symbolic, not mandatory ; The US was the only "no" vote, calling the resolution a "radical and ideological project" and objecting to language linking Mercator's distortions to colonial legacies ; Ukraine raised concerns over the depiction of Crimea, while other nations raised contested territory issues — but these were geopolitical posturing, not map issues ; African nations framed the resolution as "cognitive justice" — correcting the mental map that equates size with power and importance

item.title: How Do GPS Apps Like Google Maps Know When There's Police Ahead?
item.description: Google Maps and other GPS apps detect police sightings through crowdsourced user reports, not through any official data feed — drivers submit reports that other users confirm or deny, with Waze data also integrated into Google Maps. — Key takeaways: Google Maps relies on crowdsourced user reports for police sightings, not official data feeds ; When a driver reports police, the report appears on the maps of other users on the same road ; Other drivers can confirm whether the police sighting is still valid, keeping reports up to date ; Google Maps also integrates police report data from Waze, which Google owns ; Waze rewards users with points for submitting reports, creating a larger dataset for Google Maps ; Users can submit reports via the "Report" icon in navigation mode on smartphone, Android Auto, or Apple CarPlay ; Reports are temporary and evolve with the situation — they are not permanent markers ; The feature raises concerns about helping drivers evade checkpoints, but also helps with speed awareness and safety

item.title: Wildfire Map Spotlight: Indonesia Forest and Peatland Fires
item.description: Indonesia is experiencing its most intense wildfire season in 11 years, with forest and peatland fires burning across 1.36 million hectares by August 2026, concentrated in Kalimantan and Sumatra, producing massive smoke haze that has affected over 12.5 million people and spread to Malaysia and Singapore. — Key takeaways: Indonesia's 2026 wildfire season is the most intense in 11 years, driven by a strong El Niño and positive Indian Ocean Dipole ; Cumulative burned area reached 1,358,714 hectares by August 31, with 1.32 million hectares burned in August alone ; Peatland fires account for ~447,600 hectares and produce 3x more fine particles and 5x more sulfur dioxide than conventional forest fires ; Over 12.5 million people across seven Indonesian provinces have been exposed to haze, with respiratory infections doubling to 113,336 cases by September 9 ; 688 high-confidence hotspots detected on September 11, with Central Kalimantan recording 271 alone ; Indonesia deployed 53 aircraft across six priority provinces, and Japan delivered three CH-47 Chinook helicopters plus 180 personnel ; 19.7 million metric tons of fire-related emissions in the first week of September alone — the highest of any country globally that week

item.title: IBM and NASA Release Open-Source AI Model for Lunar Surface Mapping
item.description: IBM and NASA have released the open-source NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model, an AI foundation model trained on decades of lunar observation data that outperforms widely used methods by up to 23% in identifying key geographic features on the Moon's surface, including potential ice deposits, craters, and volcanic formations. — Key takeaways: The NASA-IBM Lunar Foundation Model is one of the first publicly available foundation models for scientific exploration of the Moon, now available on Hugging Face ; The model exceeds widely used methods by up to 23% in identifying key geographic features including potential ice deposits, craters, and volcanic formations ; It reduced error (RMSE) in identifying areas with high potential for lunar ice up to 22% compared to the SwinV2-B (ImageNet) model ; At context-scale resolution (~100 meters), it outperforms SwinV2-B by nearly 19% using just half the training data ; The model was trained on a unified, machine learning-ready lunar dataset aggregating over 30 spatially-aligned layers from nine instruments across four missions (LRO, GRAIL, SELENE/Kaguya) ; It joins the Prithvi family of open foundation models, spanning geospatial, weather, heliophysics, and now lunar science ; Crater mapping with the model helps NASA select safe landing sites, avoid hazards, and plan long-term lunar infrastructure

item.title: Google Maps Is Now Terrible: Explained
item.description: The Drive explains why Google Maps and similar navigation apps have gotten worse at saving time: mass adoption of GPS routing means too many users are sent down the same alternate routes, creating a Nash equilibrium where individual optimization degrades collective outcomes — and there is no easy fix. — Key takeaways: An estimated 7 billion devices worldwide rely on GPS, from phones to golf balls ; A 2019 study found that between 2007 and 2017, services like Google Maps saved 52 billion gallons of fuel and a trillion miles through more efficient routing ; GPS adoption has generated an estimated $1.4 trillion in economic benefits since the 1980s ; The core problem: routing apps don't track how many users they've sent on a given route and can't know where competitor services are sending users ; When everyone uses the same app to avoid traffic, alternate routes become congested too, negating the benefit ; This creates a Nash equilibrium where individual route optimization degrades collective traffic outcomes ; There is no simple solution — the problem is structural to how decentralized routing works at scale

item.title: Google Maps Has a Private Navigation Mode — But It Doesn't Make You Invisible
item.description: L'Automobile Magazine explains Google Maps' little-known private navigation mode (mode navigation privée), which suspends recording of searches, routes, and visited locations — but warns that it does not make the user invisible, as location data is still transmitted for navigation purposes. — Key takeaways: Google Maps memorizes searches, routes, and visited locations by default, feeding personalized recommendations ; The private navigation mode (mode navigation privée) suspends recording of activity in the user's Google account during the session ; Comparable to a browser's incognito mode: searches and trips are not saved, and activity is not used for personalized recommendations ; On Android and iPhone: tap profile photo → select "Activer le mode navigation privée" ; Personalization features that depend on location history become unavailable during private navigation ; The mode does NOT make the user invisible: GPS location is still used for navigation, and mobile operators and third parties may still collect data ; Timeline (historique de trajets), location permissions, and GPS battery consumption are separate settings that can be managed independently

item.title: Google Explains the Disappearing Speedometer in Maps on Android Auto
item.description: Google has explained that the disappearing speedometer in Google Maps on Android Auto is not a bug but a rollout issue: the ability to view the speedometer, speed limit, and traffic signs without a destination set is still rolling out gradually, and users need to set a destination for the features to appear in the meantime. — Key takeaways: Google Maps on Android Auto gained a live speedometer feature earlier in 2026, but users recently reported it had vanished ; Google confirmed the speedometer rollout is proceeding normally — the issue is that viewing it without a destination set is a separate feature still rolling out ; Users need to set a destination for the speedometer, speed limit, and traffic signals/stop signs to appear ; Android Authority alum and current Googler Mishaal Rahman confirmed the explanation after speaking with the Android Auto product team ; The "disappearances" were not a bug but rather the absence of a not-yet-fully-deployed feature for destination-free display

item.title: Geo Sessions 2026: From Data Collection to Operational Intelligence
item.description: NV5's Geo Sessions 2026 virtual event highlights a fundamental shift in the geospatial industry: the challenge is no longer collecting data but turning it into operational intelligence, with AI connecting multiple remote sensing technologies into seamless decision-support workflows. — Key takeaways: NV5's Geo Sessions 2026 is a global virtual event focused on the practical application of geospatial technologies, attracting several thousand registrants from 100+ countries ; The industry has "largely solved the collection problem" — commercial satellites, drones, and airborne sensors generate unprecedented amounts of data ; The real challenge is now helping decision makers understand what matters and what action they should take ; The event features dedicated sessions on SAR, spectral imaging, lidar, and new for 2026, GeoAI ; AI is accelerating the evolution by creating new opportunities to connect geospatial data, automate workflows, and surface insights that previously required significant manual effort ; Over 20 international speakers with live panel discussions and audience Q&A ; The event is free to attend with sessions available on demand afterwards

item.title: A New UN Resolution Takes a Step Toward Decolonizing World Maps
item.description: A geography professor argues that the UN's "Correct the Map" resolution is a meaningful step toward decolonizing cartography, but notes that online platforms like Google Maps still use the Web Mercator projection, limiting the resolution's practical impact on everyday mapping. — Key takeaways: The UN resolution (A/RES/80/297) was adopted 164-1 with 6 abstentions; the US was the sole opponent ; The Mercator projection's distortions were known for centuries but only politically challenged in the 1970s, beginning with Arno Peters' equal-area map ; The Equal Earth projection (2018) is positioned as a less controversial alternative to the Gall-Peters projection ; Web Mercator remains the default for Google Maps and similar platforms, perpetuating the same distortions the UN resolution seeks to correct ; Online maps don't just reproduce Mercator's size distortions — they also structure worldviews around road networks, business accessibility, and consumption ; Maps are "instruments of power" that influence how we see and interact with the world, not neutral representations

item.title: After Google Maps, Simon Weckert Now Targets AI Cameras With "Digital Camouflage" Shirt
item.description: Six years after tricking Google Maps with 99 smartphones to fake a Berlin traffic jam, artist Simon Weckert has created a "Digital Camouflage" shirt that uses adversarial patterns to make its wearer invisible to AI-powered surveillance cameras. — Key takeaways: Weckert's "Digital Camouflage" shirt uses psychedelic patterns designed to defeat YOLO object detection algorithms ; The technique uses "adversarial attacks" — the pattern is iteratively modified until the algorithm's confidence in detecting a person drops below threshold ; The project is a response to 30 new AI-assisted surveillance cameras installed at Kottbusser Tor in Berlin's Kreuzberg district ; The cameras are not yet active; their activation is expected after Berlin's September 20 election ; Weckert's 2020 "Google Maps hack" used 99 smartphones in a cart to create a fake traffic jam on Google Maps in Berlin ; The new project shifts from manipulating cartographic data to exposing the fragility of AI vision systems

item.title: Overture Maps Points of Interest: 60 Million POIs from Open Data
item.description: Meta AI highlights the Overture Maps Foundation's points-of-interest dataset, which comprises nearly 60 million POIs worldwide — data not previously available in OpenStreetMap, released as open data for mapping and geospatial applications. — Key takeaways: The Overture Maps Foundation's POI layer contains nearly 60 million points of interest ; These POIs are data not previously available in OpenStreetMap, adding significant new coverage ; The dataset is part of Overture Maps' mission to create a comprehensive, interoperable open map of the world ; Overture Maps combines data from Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, TomTom, and the Linux Foundation ; The POI layer supports applications in navigation, local search, urban planning, and commercial analytics

item.title: Waze Dethroned? Drivers Now Prefer Google Maps for Navigation
item.description: A MarketWatch study shows Google Maps has overtaken Waze as the most-used GPS app among US drivers (70%), driven by its intuitive interface, real-time traffic prediction, and Google's ongoing integration of Waze's best community features. — Key takeaways: Google Maps is used by 70% of US drivers for radar avoidance, compared to 27% for Waze and 25% for Apple Maps ; Even iPhone users in the US prefer Google Maps over Apple's native Maps app ; Google has been gradually merging Waze's best features into Google Maps, including community alerts for police controls and incidents ; In France, Google Maps cannot display radar warnings due to legal restrictions (Code de la route Article R. 413-15), giving Waze and TomTom AmiGo an advantage ; Waze has faced criticism for connectivity issues and less relevant routing over the past year ; Google plans to add more incident types (accidents, road hazards, construction) to Google Maps community alerts

item.title: TomTom AmiGo Becomes New Map Option for Android Auto
item.description: TomTom AmiGo has launched as a new navigation option for Android Auto, offering a free, ad-free alternative to Google Maps and Waze with community-powered speed camera alerts, real-time traffic, and a cleaner interface. — Key takeaways: TomTom AmiGo is now available as a navigation app for Android Auto, offering an alternative to Google Maps and Waze ; The app provides community-powered real-time alerts for fixed and mobile speed cameras, accidents, roadblocks, and speed limits ; TomTom AmiGo is completely free and ad-free, unlike TomTom's premium subscription services ; The app features a cleaner, more minimalist interface than its competitors, showing only essential driving information ; TomTom AmiGo has been available in Brazil since 2017 as a standalone mobile app ; The expansion to Android Auto follows Sygic as the first third-party navigation app on Google's car platform

item.title: TomTom Adds Knowledge Management and AI to Orbis Maps
item.description: TomTom is transforming its Orbis Maps platform into a spatial knowledge layer for AI agents, adding contextual data, AI assistant capabilities, and an MCP server that lets AI models query location intelligence for complex spatial reasoning tasks. — Key takeaways: TomTom Orbis Maps combines OpenStreetMap, Overture Maps, TomTom's own data, and vehicle sensor data — over 5 billion data points ; TomTom has stored 2.8 trillion kilometres of worldwide distance data and trillions of GPS points ; Orbis is being positioned as a "spatial knowledge layer" for AI agents, enabling natural-language spatial queries ; TomTom has released Orbis APIs and an MCP server for AI agent integration ; The TomTom AI Assistant (TAIA) works at the front end, while the Agent Toolkit enables third-party AI agents to access spatial intelligence ; Use cases include insurers querying flood-damage proximity, city planners analyzing travel-time changes, and fleet managers rerouting vehicles ; Orbis Lane Model Maps provide lane-level geometry for autonomous driving applications

item.title: Japan, India, Ukraine: Why Some Countries Are Uneasy About the New UN Map
item.description: Following the UN's adoption of the Equal Earth projection, Japan, India, and Ukraine have raised concerns — not about the projection itself, but about how the new map depicts their disputed territories through colour shading and border delineation. — Key takeaways: Japan objects to the Equal Earth map using the same colour for the disputed Kuril Islands as for Russian territory ; India demands that Kashmir be depicted "in accordance with India's official map," rejecting any "inaccurate or misleading depiction" ; Ukraine abstained from the vote, arguing the map's shading of Crimea legitimizes Russia's 2014 annexation ; None of the three countries oppose the Equal Earth projection itself — they contest how their disputed territories are rendered ; Japan has formally asked Equal Earth's creators to change the map through its embassy in the US ; The six abstentions (Estonia, Georgia, Moldova, Serbia, Lithuania, Ukraine) all voted in solidarity with Ukraine over Crimea

item.title: "Correct the Map" Resolution: From Cartographic Question to Cultural and Political Issue
item.description: In an interview with Africa Radio, Speak Up Africa co-founder Fara Ndiaye discusses the UN's adoption of the "Correct the Map" resolution, arguing that cartographic representation is not merely a technical issue but a cultural and political one that shapes how generations perceive the world. — Key takeaways: The "Correct the Map" campaign was launched by NGOs Africa No Filter and Speak Up Africa, co-founded by Fara Ndiaye ; The campaign does not exclusively promote Equal Earth — it advocates ending the default use of Mercator, and would accept any equal-area projection ; Equal Earth was chosen partly because it is free to use and less controversial than the Gall-Peters projection ; 164 countries voted in favor — described as "not Africa against Western countries, but 164 countries against one" ; The campaign's next phase focuses on working with education ministries to update school textbooks ; The resolution also calls on UN agencies to update their working documents to use equal-area projections as the default ; Ndiaye emphasizes the issue affects not just Africa but also Latin America and South Asia, whose surfaces are particularly reduced on Mercator

item.title: Mapping Silicate Minerals From Space
item.description: NASA-funded scientists have created the first global maps of silicate, sulfate, and carbonate minerals in Earth's arid regions using thermal infrared spectroscopy data from the ECOSTRESS and ASTER satellite sensors, enabling space-based identification of mineral resources including lithium-bearing rocks. — Key takeaways: Researchers created 1-kilometer resolution global maps of silicate, sulfate, and carbonate minerals using ECOSTRESS (ISS) and ASTER (Terra satellite) thermal infrared data ; Thermal infrared spectroscopy is the only known method to detect silica from space, using each mineral's unique spectral signature ; Silicate deposits are associated with lithium-bearing minerals used in batteries, making the maps valuable for resource exploration ; Silicate alteration on the surface can also indicate underground geothermal activity, pointing to potential renewable energy sites ; The maps were validated by comparing satellite observations with field data from sites in California, New Mexico, and Morocco ; The data complement NASA's EMIT sensor, which detects oxides, sulfides, and clays associated with precious minerals ; The dataset is publicly available through NASA's Earthdata Search and the Land Processes DAAC as GeoTIFF

item.title: Apple Maps Caught in "New America" Toponymy Controversy Over New Mexico
item.description: New Mexico's congressional delegation has asked Apple and Google to commit to keeping the state's name on their maps, preempting potential "New America" renaming after social media posts by the US president suggested the change. — Key takeaways: Democratic representatives from New Mexico wrote to Apple and Google asking them not to rename their state "New America" in mapping services ; The request follows social media posts by President Trump suggesting the name change, though no official measure has been taken ; Apple Maps and Google Maps rely on the federal Geographic Names Information System (GNIS) for US place names ; Previous GNIS updates (Gulf of Mexico, Lake Ontario) were reflected in Apple Maps after presidential decrees modified entries ; Google Maps applied the Lake Ontario name change immediately upon the decree's signing; Apple Maps updated after GNIS was updated ; The episode highlights how digital mapping has become a concrete terrain for political decisions

item.title: TomTom and citiEU Strengthen Ties to Deliver Advanced Traffic Monitoring and Location Analytics
item.description: TomTom announced an expanded partnership with citiEU to deliver advanced location analytics, traffic intelligence, and mobility solutions across Europe and the Middle East, leveraging TomTom's full product portfolio including Traffic Analytics. — Key takeaways: citiEU will leverage TomTom's location intelligence to support advanced location analytics, traffic intelligence, and mobility solutions ; The expanded agreement covers clients in Europe and the Middle East ; citiEU will use a broad portfolio of TomTom products including Traffic Analytics, traffic volumes, and routing data ; The partnership was announced September 10, 2026 from Amsterdam ; TomTom positions itself as "the specialist in mapping and location technology" ; Multiple financial and trade outlets covered the announcement (Yahoo Finance, Zonebourse, TradingView, Barchart)

item.title: Xpeng Integrates Google Maps Into Its Embedded Navigation
item.description: Chinese automaker Xpeng has integrated Google Maps cartographic data and navigation capabilities directly into its embedded vehicle navigation system — not as an app, but as a native integration of Google's mapping data. — Key takeaways: Google Maps data arrives natively in Xpeng vehicles, not as a standalone application ; Xpeng integrates Google's cartographic data and navigational APIs for the first time ; This makes Xpeng the first Chinese automaker to natively integrate Google Maps data ; The integration provides real-time cartographic data and navigation features ; Previous coverage noted Xpeng's integration of Google Maps Auto SDK in August 2026
